claim.claim-text: a housing (12) that defines a port (14) that is configured and adapted to selectively and securely receive an end portion (16) of a fiber optic connector (18); and a fiber connector detection mechanism (26) configured to automatically transition the pluggable optical module (10) from a high power state when the fiber optic connector (18) is present and engaged with the port (14) to a low power state when the fiber optic connector (18) is otherwise disengaged from the port (14), thereby limiting the housing (12) temperature when the fiber optic connector (18) is disengaged from the port (14).
2. The pluggable optical module (10) as claimed in claim 1, wherein the housing (12) includes metallic surface that gets heated based on an operating state of the pluggable optical module (10).
3. The pluggable optical module (10) as claimed in any one of claims 1 to 2, wherein the fiber connector detection mechanism (12) includes a mechanical detection mechanism.

4. The pluggable optical module (10) as claimed in claim 3, wherein the mechanical detection mechanism includes a pivotable arm or push pin that is displaced by the fiber optic connector (18) when the fiber optic connector (18) is inserted into the port (14).
5. The pluggable optical module (10) as claimed in any one of claims 1 to 2, wherein the fiber connector detection mechanism (12) includes an electrical detection mechanism.

6. The pluggable optical module (10) as claimed in claim 5, wherein the electrical detection mechanism includes one or more conductive surfaces associated with an end portion (16) that are actuated based on contact.
7. The pluggable optical module (10) as claimed in any one of claims 1 to 2, wherein the fiber connector detection mechanism (12) includes a magnetic sensor.
8. The pluggable optical module (10) as claimed in any one of claims 1 to 2, wherein the fiber connector detection mechanism (12) includes an optical detection mechanism.
9. The pluggable optical module (10) as claimed in any one of claims 1 to 8, wherein the low power state includes a laser-off operating state.

10. The pluggable optical module (10) as claimed in any one of claims 1 to 9, wherein the low power state and the high power state have different levels of intensity of an optical signal from the pluggable optical module (10).

11. The pluggable optical module (10) as claimed in any one of claims 1 to 10, wherein the fiber connector detection mechanism (26) is configured to automatically transition the pluggable optical module (10) based on software-based control.
12. The pluggable optical module (10) as claimed in any one of claims 1 to 11, wherein the pluggable optical module (10) is a QSFP-DD pluggable optical module.

13. A method comprising: connecting or disconnecting the end portion (16) of the fiber optic connector (18) with the port (14) on the pluggable optical module (10) as claimed in any one of claims 1 to 12.
